subject: Velocity commit margining & tokens/sec headroom analysis
body:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@velocity.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Estimating commit for our inference peak patterns

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo — VelocityAI liked the autoscaling story. We need a concrete sizing recommendation for a potential committed Dedicated pool. High level context: our production traffic is spiky (short bursts around feature launches) but baseline is modest. Key constraints:
- Target SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end token latency <= 120ms for single-turn generation (up to 1024 tokens).
- Expected steady DAU: ~75k users, average 60 tokens/req, peak concurrency estimate 1200 concurrent requests during spikes.
- We plan to ship a generative assistant that does a 1-step generation ~80% and 2-step flows for the rest.

Can your team map this to tokens/sec, required GPU slabs, and recommended headroom for a 12-month commit? If you can surface a few commit tiers (conservative/typical/aggressive) with tokens/sec and an ops safety buffer that would be great.

Attaching our throughput trace (sanitized) — let me know if you need more.

Cheers,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
VP Product, VelocityAI

-----Original reply-----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@velocity.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Estimating commit for our inference peak patterns

Alicia — thanks, this is exactly the right ask to size a Dedicated pool. I did an initial pass with the numbers you provided and pulled a few modeling assumptions we typically use for Velocity-like workloads. Summary below; I'll loop in Marissa with the numeric sheets.

Top-line assumptions (conservative baseline):
- Avg tokens per request: 60 (you provided)
- Peak concurrent requests: 1200 (spike) => peak token-rate = 1200 * 60 = 72k tokens/sec (if all issuing simultaneously).
- Effective throughput per A100-80GB slab for your preferred model (quantized 4-bit variant) with our runtime: ~12k tokens/sec steady with p95 latency ~90-110ms depending on seq length and batching behavior.

Initial tiered recommendations (tokens/sec commit, implied slabs, ops headroom):
1) Typical tier: commit 40k tokens/sec (~3.5 slabs). Practically we'd provision 4 slabs. Expected p95=~100ms under typical spikes, 20% headroom for burst absorb.
2) Conservative tier: commit 60k tokens/sec (~5 slabs). Provision 5 slabs; target p95=~110ms with 10-15% headroom for scheduled launches.
3) Aggressive tier: commit 85k tokens/sec (~7-8 slabs). Provision 8 slabs; p95=~95-120ms with minimal additional headroom — recommended only if you need 0-failure margin on 5-10x short bursts.

Notes: the slab->tokens/sec mapping depends on model variant, sequence length distribution, and KV-cache hit rate. Your 80% single-turn usage helps since caching benefits are limited, but multi-step flows will create KV warmups that increase GPU efficiency slightly.

Attached: initial throughput model (velocity_throughput_model_v3.xlsx). Marissa — can you sanity-check the slab mapping and drop a recommended burst policy (burst pool vs. autoscale buffer)?

—Jonas

On Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -07:00, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Jonas / Alicia — quick follow-up with more concrete headroom/RPS math. I expanded the sheet and ran two scenario sims: an event spike (5x base for 3 minutes) and sustained surge (2x base for 30 minutes). Key outputs:

- Baseline calculation: your stated baseline (75k DAU) maps to ~450 requests/sec avg (assuming session distribution and daily active spread). That equals ~27k tokens/sec baseline.
- Event spike (5x): instantaneous tokens/sec ~135k. This is above any single commit tier — bursts need either pre-warmed burst capacity or fallback routing to a smaller but cheaper model.
- Recommended operational safety buffer: 25% above committed tokens/sec to allow for scheduling jitter, model rollouts, and degraded node capacity during maintenance.

Concrete recommender:
- 12-month starter commit: 35k tokens/sec (provision 3 slabs, keep 1 pre-warmed burst node pool on Dedicated for 5-minute prewarm) — cost-effective, good for gradual rollout.
- 12-month growth commit: 60k tokens/sec (provision 5 slabs, 25% buffer = ~75k tokens/sec absorb) — balances cost vs. headroom.
- 12-month enterprise commit: 90k tokens/sec (provision 8 slabs, 25% buffer = ~112k tokens/sec) — recommended if you want to avoid routing fallbacks entirely during planned campaigns.

Operational notes:
- For short 3–5 minute spikes, warm nodes via predictive pre-warm triggers (CloudWatch/EventBridge hooks from your deployment pipeline).
- For sustained surges, autoscale policies that spin up adjacent Dedicated capacity within 10–15 minutes are reasonable, but you should assume some tail latency increase while capacity ramps.

Ben — can you prepare a commit pricing sketch for the starter and growth tiers? Alicia — if you want, we can build a 2-week POC on 3-provisioned-slabs + pre-warm so you can validate p95 in your environment.

—Marissa

On Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -07:00, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:

Team / Alicia — attaching a short commit proposal that maps the three tiers to monthly committed spend and include a one-time migration/validation credit for the POC. Highlights:
- Starter (35k tokens/sec): 3 slab commit, monthly committed tokens converted to blended unit price, estimated monthly cost $18k/mo with 3-month ramp credit.
- Growth (60k tokens/sec): 5 slab commit, estimated $30k/mo with volume discount at annual billing.
- Enterprise (90k tokens/sec): 8 slab commit, estimated $43k/mo, includes 24/7 on-call add-on as optional.

I've put detailed line items in proposed_commit_terms_velocity_2027.pdf and the throughput model has the slab math if you want to tweak seq-length assumptions.

Next steps:
1) Alicia: confirm which tier(s) you want to evaluate in a POC.
2) If starter or growth, we can spin up the Dedicated POC within 5 business days.
3) We'll run a joint load test with your sanitized traces and validate p95 latency targets; if we miss SLO by >10% we will provide an extra credit toward your first invoice.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30m call to walk through the sheet.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
